chapter: Washington in the 1930s: big bands, lessons, first jobs
title: Drummer Leo Gilpoopy hires him for the Atlantic Beer Garden
summary: Just before sixteen he is recruited to play duo seven nights a week at twelve dollars a week.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So I guess it was just before my sixteenth birthday... I was standing in front of my house one day, with some of the other guys who I was playing around with. And this fellow came up and asked the crowd did they know this kid named John Malachi. They said, "Yeah, there he is right there." He said, "Are you John?" I said, "Yeah." He said, "You play the piano, right?" I said, "Yeah, I like the piano." So he says, "My name is Leo Aloysious Gilpoopy" -- which I thought was kind of funny, because I didn't know whether "Gilpoopy" was a real name or not. I thought he could have been putting me on or something. "I'm a drummer, and I'm playing at the Atlantic Beer Garden on Fourteenth Street. And someone told me about you. I want you to come up and play with me, and play this job with me." So I think I told him that I had never played with too many musicians before... I don't know what I said -- something to the effect that I didn't know many pieces or something. And he said, "That will be okay. You come on up and it will be just you and I playing" -- he played the drums and I play the piano. It was in the days when they had what they call beer gardens, when people came in -- it always seemed to me that they drank more beer than they did whiskey.
I wasn't really noticing it that much...

But anyway, I accepted this and gladly took it, because it really was my pleasure. So I started on this job. We worked seven days a week, and my salary was twelve dollars a week. I was just happy I was making... I felt like I was making good money and working!
